context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's step-01e rework (new §10 of req217-http-admission-wiring.md), fixing SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-03 double-global-consumption FAIL.
acceptance_criteria: design doc states precisely where and how the global gate's ref is released relative to the tenant gate's acquisition, with no ambiguity for ELIXIR-DEV to guess at
design doc explicitly answers whether releasing the global gate's ref before the tenant gate acquires creates a race, and states whether that is accepted behavior or a defect needing further design
design doc explicitly justifies not changing Letflow.Admission's public API, state shape, or atomicity algorithm
design doc updates the exact api_pipeline.ex plug chain order to reflect the fix
design doc flags for TEST-DESIGNER that AC3/AC4's minimum-global-cap arithmetic must be re-derived (global_cap == 1)
no implementation code (function bodies) introduced in the design doc

result.summary:
Read step-03-security-reviewer.json (original finding), step-01e-code-designer-rework.json (fix summary), and the new §10 of lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md in full (lines 516-744), then independently cross-checked every claim against the actual shipped source: lib/letflow/admission.ex (core GenServer, REQ-216) and lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex (the plug, REQ-217) in full, plus test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs's AC3/AC4 comments.

1. MECHANICS FULLY SPECIFIED. §10.1 item 1 gives release_global_ref/1 a complete @spec (Plug.Conn.t() -> Plug.Conn.t()) and an unambiguous body description: check conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref] for nil (no-op branch), else (a) call Letflow.Admission.release/1 on that exact ref, (b) remove that SPECIFIC ref from the @admission_refs_pdict_key list via List.delete/2 (not a full clear -- correct, since only the global entry is present in the list at that point in the chain), (c) assign(conn, :global_admission_ref, nil). Confirmed against the ALREADY-SHIPPED lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex that :global_admission_ref/:tenant_admission_ref are the real assign-key atoms already in use (line 159/167) and that the existing before_send callback's release_ref/1 helper (line 184) already has a release_ref(nil) -> :ok no-op clause -- so setting the assign to nil at step 5 is sufficient for mount 1's already-registered before_send (Mechanism A) to safely no-op later, with zero code change needed in admit/3. §10.1 item 5 explicitly states Mechanism B (release_pending_refs/0, confirmed to iterate-and-clear the pdict list exactly as described at lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex:207-213) will typically drain a list containing only the tenant ref past step 5, and that this needs no special-casing since it already iterates whatever remains. Both Mechanism A and B interactions are stated explicitly, not left to accident. Confirmed the design's claim of Letflow.Admission.release/2's own documented idempotency (admission.ex moduledoc + handle_call({:release,...}) Map.pop-based no-op branch) backs the 'double-release is harmless regardless' framing, but the design does not rely on that safety net for the normal path -- it does the surgical List.delete/2 + assign-to-nil precisely to avoid needing it, which is the more careful design choice.

2. RACE-CONDITION ACCEPTANCE IS WELL-REASONED -- independently verified, not just trusted. Read lib/letflow/admission.ex's moduledoc myself: it does state, per-call, 'There is no wait queue: try_acquire/2 is a single synchronous decision against current state, never parked' -- this is a genuine, pre-existing (REQ-216) documented property, not invented for this rework, and it does support treating two try_acquire/2 calls (even from the same request) as never specially linked -- REQ-216's design never had a concept of a caller 'reserving across calls'. Reason (2) ('tracks real connection-holding time more accurately') also holds: AuthPipeline's own DB work (token verification, tenant resolution, JIT provisioning) completes and returns its connection to the pool before AuthPipeline's plug returns control to the pipeline -- by the time release_global_ref/1 runs (immediately after AuthPipeline), this request genuinely holds no DB connection, so releasing the global unit at that instant reflects reality more accurately than the original bug's 'hold it through the whole remaining request' behavior, which is the OPPOSITE of accurate. Reason (3) (no differential starvation) is also correct: Letflow.Admission is a single GenServer with one mailbox: a freed unit is contested via ordinary FIFO-by-arrival GenServer.call/2 semantics identical for every caller, this request included -- nothing in admission.ex privileges or penalizes a caller based on prior grants. My independent judgment: this reasoning is sound and the race is correctly classified as ordinary admission-control behavior (a request can always lose a fresh capacity check), not a new defect. It is a real, disclosed trade -- a request can now pay AuthPipeline's cost and still be rejected at the tenant gate -- but that is precisely the kind of visible, honestly-stated limitation this project's own convention (decision 0014 precedent, cited in the requirement text) treats as acceptable when named rather than hidden, and §10.3's moduledoc obligation ensures it is named in the shipped code, not just the design doc.

3. NO REQ-216 API/CONTRACT CHANGE NEEDED -- confirmed by reading lib/letflow/admission.ex's public functions myself: start_link/1, try_acquire/2, release/2 (default server \\ __MODULE__, so callable as release/1) are the complete public surface, all unchanged. release_global_ref/1 is a NEW function on Letflow.Plugs.Admission (the REQ-217 plug module), not on Letflow.Admission (the REQ-216 core module) -- it composes entirely from the existing release/1 call (same default-arg arity already exposed), no new core function, no new state field, no change to the atomicity algorithm in handle_call({:try_acquire, ...}). §10.2's rejected alternative (opt-out-of-composing or ref-transfer) was correctly identified as the ONLY path that would have required a core API change, and correctly rejected in favor of the plug-only fix.

4. NO NEW CORRECTNESS GAP -- traced the plug chain step by step myself against §10.1 item 4's three named paths plus the shipped code: (a) global gate rejects outright -> halts at mount 1, release_global_admission never reached, nothing acquired, nothing to release -- consistent. (b) global gate admits, AuthPipeline itself halts (auth failure) -> conn.halted short-circuits Plug.Builder's chain before reaching the new plug, so mount 1's original before_send still fires on AuthPipeline's own halt+response, releasing the global ref the ORIGINAL way -- the tenant gate is never reached, no double-consumption exists on this path, and release_global_ref never runs so no premature-nil-assign race applies here either. (c) global gate admits, then a raise before reaching the new plug -> Mechanism B (release_pending_refs/0) drains the pdict list, which at that point holds only the global ref (tenant mount never ran) -- released once, correctly. (d) both gates run to completion -> traced above in point 1, no double-release, no missed release, no wrong-ref release. Found no scenario producing an inconsistent state.

5. NO LITERAL IMPLEMENTATION CODE -- verified directly: grepped for all ``` fences in the file (6 total, at lines 190/195, 294/296, 555/557) -- the only fence pair inside §10 is the 555-557 pair, and its content is exclusively `@spec release_global_ref(Plug.Conn.t()) :: Plug.Conn.t()`, a type signature, not a function body. All of §10's actual mechanics (the nil-check, List.delete/2, assign-to-nil, mount position) are described in prose, matching this doc's own established post-rework convention. PASS.

6. TEST-DESIGNER FOLLOW-UP ACCURATELY DESCRIBED -- read test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs directly: AC3's and AC4's own comments (lines 165-171, 196-198) state verbatim that global_cap == 2 is 'the smallest value that admits even ONE full request' under the current (buggy) wiring. Under §10.1's fix, at no point does one request hold two global units simultaneously (confirmed via the step-by-step trace in point 4), so global_cap == 1 is sufficient for the same single-request scenario -- §10.4's flagged re-derivation is correct and necessary, and correctly scoped as a TEST-DESIGNER task rather than resolved in the design doc itself.

No gaps found across any of the six checks. This design is unambiguous enough to build from as-is.
